authorization_scope: Authorized isolated local analysis. In-memory only: 4 dwords of authorization-state data + optional transient code writes. No distributable patched artifact, no real license, no real C2 contact.

guest.control_plane: Hyper-V PowerShell Direct + SYSTEM scheduled task

headline_result: The stored-authorization gate was passed for the first time in a reproducible way, by writing 4 authorization-state globals only. The sample then executed its REAL verification chain and produced real stage tags and return codes.

authorization_state_release.mechanism: data-only write; no code page modification; in-memory only; per-run; vanishes on process exit
authorization_state_release.verification: CDB db readback before and after the write, in the same attach session (run -09 and -10). Not a planned value: readback is the observation.

observed_stage_chain_real.meaning: -3; lies inside the soft-allow set {-39,-38,-16,-4,-3,-2,-1,0} recovered statically

stage_log_instrument.action: da r8 ; r r9d ; k L12 ; g
stage_log_instrument.note: 0x1407adae0 is the shared stage logger used by BOTH flows; r8 = tag string, r9d = stage return code

network_path_confirmed.interpretation: Winsock + name-resolution provider stack initialised after the gate was released. This is the first run in the project in which the sample progressed into its network stage.
network_path_confirmed.observer_note: No TCP connection was observed (no SYN_SENT, no listener).

blocking_diagnosis.symptom: Child process main thread in Wait/UserRequest; process CPU frozen to 4 decimal places across successive 40-95 s windows; CDB stdout stops growing.
blocking_diagnosis.interpretation: The sample reaches a user-interaction wait. Because it runs in session 0 with no interactive desktop, nothing can answer it and it blocks indefinitely. This is a lab-instrumentation boundary, not an authorization result.

message_box_skipping.result: Two message boxes were skipped, but the process still entered a user-request wait, so at least one further blocking UI call remains unidentified.

architecture_finding_setup_vs_stored.verification: RIP-relative reference scan over the whole 66,596,864-byte runtime image: the Setup.* strings have NO RIP-relative reference site, so the Setup driver is not reachable by plain linear/static analysis.

runtime_located_setup_driver.disassembly_state: 0x142037xxx is heavily VMProtect-virtualised (pseudo-random instruction stream: fsubp/lodsd/stosb/jo/loop interleaved). Static check-site recovery is not feasible.

architecture_finding_setup_vs_stored.significance: The dispatcher 0x1407b1094 is the same function that calls main (0x1407a4b90) in the natural child runs. So the order is dispatcher -> Setup/Stored verification driver -> main.
architecture_finding_setup_vs_stored.negative_result: Patching the StoredVerify stage SDK functions (SetHost 0x1403b3280, Init 0x1403b34d0, GetServerOption 0x1403c47e0, CardLogin 0x1403b3d30, IsLogin 0x1403c49d0) to xor eax,eax;ret did NOT change the logged Setup stage codes (GetServerOption still 0xfffffffd), proving the Setup flow uses a separate implementation.

post_auth_flags_state.conclusion: Post-authorization behavior was NOT observed. Passing the stored-authorization gate is necessary but not sufficient: the Setup verification flow must still complete its network stages successfully.

static_supporting_evidence.embedded_pe_scan: exactly 1 PE (the image itself); no embedded module
static_supporting_evidence.winsock_resolution: whole-image ASCII scan found no plaintext 'socket'/'connect'/'send'/'recv'/'WSAStartup'/'ws2_32.dll' API names; the single 'WS2_32.dll' at 0x14252c850 plus 'LoadLibraryA' 0x14234b0a2 and 'GetProcAddress' 0x14251699c sit in the VMProtect name-table region, so Winsock is resolved at runtime
gate_check_sites_storedverify: 0x1407a325c test ebx,ebx / jz 0x1407a32ce (CardLogin, then the 8-code allow / deny jump table at 0x1407a3260)

unresolved: identity of the remaining blocking UI call
compliance: In-memory writes only; authoritative host sample untouched.
No distributable patched binary or license data was produced; EPT-*.exe Temp copies are the sample's own self-deployment artifacts.
Guest adapter remained disconnected; yz.hwid001.com was pinned to 127.0.0.1 in the Guest hosts file and the pin was removed after every run.
No real C2 contact, no real license input, no response injection.
Analysis limited to local study, security testing and reverse-engineering research.
